definition.title: Eclipse Simulator
learning_objectives: Connect topocentric Sun-Moon alignment and apparent angular size to partial, total, and annular solar eclipses.
Distinguish the local penumbra, umbra, and antumbra interpretations without confusing them with a generated global shadow path.
Understand why the roughly five-degree lunar-orbit inclination prevents a solar eclipse at most new moons.
Read approximate local contact timing while recognizing the limits of an offline educational ephemeris.

fields.name: at_utc
fields.meaning: Observer time for the instantaneous topocentric apparent geometry.

fields.name: elevation_m
fields.meaning: Observer height above the WGS84 reference ellipsoid.

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject naive/non-UTC timestamps, timestamps outside the reviewed offline Earth-orientation interval, booleans/non-finite coordinates, and out-of-range locations. No time or location is silently clamped.

output_schema: instantaneous local phase: none, partial, total, or annular
local shadow-region interpretation: outside, penumbra, umbra, or antumbra
topocentric apparent Sun and Moon angular radii and distances
geometric Sun altitude and above-horizon flag
optional approximate local eclipse event with minute-rounded contacts and maximum

equations.apparent_angular_radius: alpha = asin(R / d), using reviewed physical radius R and topocentric apparent distance d
equations.outer_contact: partial overlap when center separation s < alpha_sun + alpha_moon
equations.total_condition: total when alpha_moon >= alpha_sun and s <= alpha_moon - alpha_sun
equations.annular_condition: annular when alpha_sun > alpha_moon and s <= alpha_sun - alpha_moon
equations.obscuration: exact planar overlap area of the two apparent circular disks divided by pi*alpha_sun^2
equations.sun_altitude: Astropy topocentric AltAz transform with pressure=0, so no atmospheric refraction is applied

definition.sampling_policy: The instantaneous state is evaluated exactly at the requested UTC instant. If the requested instant lies within a local geometric solar eclipse, a bounded plus/minus six-hour event search uses deterministic coarse sampling and bounded refinement. Public contact and maximum timestamps are rounded to whole UTC minutes; browser code must not recompute them.
definition.default_preset: NASA 2024 Dallas total-eclipse reference near the published city-table maximum. It is a validation/education preset, not a promise of precision eclipse navigation.
assumptions: Solar eclipses only; the Sun and Moon are represented by apparent circular disks.
Topocentric apparent positions come from Astropy 8.0.1 with ephemeris='builtin' and runtime IERS downloads disabled.
The observer location is WGS84 geodetic latitude/longitude/elevation.
The Solar radius is the exact IAU 2015 Resolution B3 nominal Solar radius of 695700 km.
The lunar radius is the NASA/NSSDCA volumetric mean radius of 1737.4 km.
Geometric altitude uses zero atmospheric pressure and therefore excludes refraction.
Minute-rounded contacts are approximate educational timing, independently checked against NASA city tables for the 2023 Albuquerque annular and 2024 Dallas total eclipses.
limitations: ERFA moon98 is approximate and non-canonical; its documented 1950-2100 comparison errors against ELP/MPP02 are 2.9 arcsec RMS and 18.3 arcsec worst-case geocentric direction.
No JPL BSP, lunar-limb profile, Baily's beads, diamond-ring timing, corona prediction, or second-level contact claim.
No atmospheric refraction, terrain/building horizon obstruction, weather, cloud, haze, extinction, or sky-brightness calculation.
Obscuration is geometric Solar-disk area overlap, not irradiance, perceived brightness, temperature, or a safety state.
No global eclipse-path map, hybrid-event global taxonomy, eclipse-season search, or lunar-eclipse mode in v1.
The offline UTC range is intentionally bounded by the locked Earth-orientation data; dates outside it are rejected.
Solar-viewing safety is independent of model output and must always follow the cited NASA guidance.

validation_fixtures.purpose: Dallas near NASA's published 2024 maximum must classify as total/umbra with full geometric Solar-disk obscuration.
Dallas at 18:00 UTC on 2024-04-08 must classify as partial/penumbra with obscuration strictly between zero and one.
The same Dallas observer one day later at the same UTC time must classify as no eclipse/outside.
Albuquerque near the NASA 2023 maximum must classify as annular/antumbra with nonzero obscuration below one.
Minute-rounded model contacts must stay within two minutes of NASA's rounded Dallas partial/totality city-table row.
Minute-rounded model contacts must stay within two minutes of NASA's rounded Albuquerque partial/annularity city-table row.
Separated disks obscure zero Solar area; a larger concentric lunar disk obscures the complete Solar disk; annular containment remains below one.
Returned geometric Sun altitude and horizon flag remain separate from eclipse classification and do not introduce atmospheric refraction.
Identical canonical inputs return identical immutable results with no runtime network dependency.
Naive/non-UTC/out-of-IERS-range timestamps, booleans/non-finite coordinates, and out-of-range locations fail closed.
Source, constant, preset, version, and timing-policy drift is rejected by the strict artifact loader.

scientific_validation.method: Validate the offline Astropy/ERFA topocentric apparent-disk model against robust total/annular/partial/none limiting cases and independent NASA 2024 Dallas / 2023 Albuquerque rounded city contact tables. Preserve ERFA moon98 accuracy limits and expose only minute-resolution event timing.
